sentences.text: Cryptarcus is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur that lived in the middle Campanian of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Alberta.
Its skull is marked by a deep notch on the rear edge of the parietal frill and a dome-shaped ornament along that notch.
The frill extends to about 120 % of the skull’s length, making it proportionally larger than in many relatives.
Each squamosal bone carries eight small spikes called episquamosals, while only three epiparietal bones are present on the frill.
The holotype skull measures roughly 94 centimetres, but the remainder of the skeleton has not been recovered.
Eight episquamosal spikes per squamosal make its frill unusually ornamented.
The species was originally described in 1940 by Charles Mortram Sternberg under the name Chasmosaurus russelli.
In 2026 Holmes, Mallon, Ryan and Evans established the new genus Cryptarcus and republished the name in the Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences.
A 2026 study re-prepared the holotype to reveal details hidden by earlier plaster reconstruction.
Additional material, a partial parietal (TMP 2013.019.0038), was later identified as belonging to the same species.
Cryptarcus was a large, quadrupedal herbivore that fed on plants.
Its massive skull and extensive frill suggest a robust head structure supporting strong jaw muscles for cropping vegetation.
Cryptarcus belongs to the chasmosaurine subfamily of ceratopsids and was erected as a new genus separate from Chasmosaurus.
Its exact relationships are uncertain; some analyses link it more closely with Utahceratops and Pentaceratops, while others keep it near Chasmosaurus.
A 2026 phylogenetic reassessment explored different weighting schemes, producing conflicting placements for the taxon.
Further studies have shown that the holotype cannot be definitively assigned as nearer to either Chasmosaurus or Pentaceratops, depending on the analytical method used.
Cryptarcus fossils come from the Dinosaur Park Formation, a Late Cretaceous (Campanian) deposit in Alberta, Canada.
Earlier views placed Chasmosaurus russelli in lower strata of the Dinosaur Park Formation, but later work showed its quarry lies in higher layers.
In 2010 Nick Longrich suggested many specimens attributed to C. russelli actually belong to Mojoceratops perifania, a proposal that most researchers have rejected.
Phylogenetic analyses give inconsistent results, with some iterations grouping Cryptarcus with Pentaceratops and others with Chasmosaurus.
Recent ideas proposing an evolutionary sequence from Cryptarcus russelli through Pentaceratops toward Terminocavus are not supported by the presented phylogenetic data.
